title: Prehabilitation before joint surgery when you are frail (UK)
meta_title: Prehabilitation before joint surgery when you are frail (UK)
meta_description: How to prepare body and home before hip or knee surgery when frail: strength exercises, nutrition, medicines, smoking and planning for coming home.
excerpt: How to prepare body and home before hip or knee surgery when frail: strength exercises, nutrition, medicines, smoking and planning for coming home.
direct_answer: Prehabilitation means getting as fit as possible before surgery. For frail people with arthritis, it can include strength and balance exercises, good nutrition, medicine review and planning help at home. Ask your surgical team about local programmes.
author: Louis Maxwell
reviewer_credentials: First Contact Practitioner, HCPC PH128483, CSP member
keywords: prehabilitation, before surgery, hip replacement, knee replacement, frailty, strength, arthritis, UK
content:
Waiting for surgery can be a chance to prepare.

This guide covers practical preparation. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Strength and balance

  • Sit-to-stand exercises.
  • Seated leg strengthening.
  • Walking as able.
  • Ask a physiotherapist for a safe plan.

Nutrition

Eat enough protein and stay hydrated. Ask about help if you are losing weight.

Health checks

  • Ask for a medicines review.
  • Stop smoking and cut down alcohol.
  • Manage diabetes and blood pressure.

Planning for home

  • Arrange help for the first weeks.
  • Set up a bed, chair and toilet that are easy to use.
  • Ask about equipment.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Will exercise make my joint worse?

Gentle exercise is usually safe; ask your team.

Is it too late to start?

Even a few weeks can help.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Hip replacement
  • NHS: Knee replacement
  • NHS: Strength exercises
  • NHS: Malnutrition
